headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default data-leak and conflict risks; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise reads uploaded files and server filesystem content, and marketingskills explicitly builds on shared context and references files/skills. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Flowise outputs are fed into marketingskills without sanitization. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Flowise outputs are copied into marketingskills prompts or skill files without filtering, injected instructions can be executed.
IF shared-context files are writable by both agents, attacker-controlled text can persist across runs.
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation rule in the handoff.
Strip or escape markdown, HTML, and tool directives before passing content.
Review shared files for prompt-like text before each run.
Use a read-only export for Flowise outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise can read server filesystem and uploaded files and has broad network egress to model providers and HTTP tools; marketingskills reads and writes local skill/context files and calls GitHub/marketing-skills.com. If sensitive chatflow inputs or marketing context are shared, either agent can expose them through external calls or persisted files. The default blast radius includes exfiltration and durable leakage.
conditions: IF chatflow inputs contain secrets or customer data and are placed into shared files, both agents can persist them.
IF Flowise tools send those inputs to model providers or HTTP tools, the data can leave the environment.
IF marketingskills writes shared context files, sensitive content can be retained beyond the session.
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared filesystem paths.
Disable or restrict HTTP tools in Flowise flows handling secrets.
Store marketing context in a separate, access-controlled directory.
Review outbound destinations before each run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries and retention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write_filesystem and read_filesystem, and Flowise uses server-datastore shared state while marketingskills writes skill/context files. With overlapping mutable surfaces and no locking documented, concurrent runs can overwrite each other or corrupt shared artifacts. Because the conflict can affect persistent workflow state, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore key, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
IF Flowise instances share server datastore entries with marketingskills-managed files, concurrent edits can race.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Back up shared artifacts before concurrent runs.
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise produces chatflow outputs and marketingskills builds on shared context, so one agent's text can become the other's input. However, marketingskills is a marketing skill set rather than an autonomous action executor, so the blast radius is mainly incorrect content propagation rather than direct external action. The pathway exists in default workflows but is not clearly authoritative by default.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes Flowise-generated text as authoritative context, errors can propagate into downstream marketing outputs.
IF Flowise flows are configured to emit unverified facts into shared context files, those facts can be reused unchanged.
mitigations: Add a human review step before reuse of generated text.
Require source links for factual claims in shared context.
Mark generated content as untrusted in filenames or headers.
Limit shared context to summaries, not raw outputs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and can store files on the server filesystem, while marketingskills handles marketing content and product marketing context. No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance risk is supportable from the profiles. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of shared content.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into both agents' shared files, retention and residency policies must be checked.
IF one agent's logs retain content longer than the other, deletion requests may be inconsistent.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared marketing workflows.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Delete shared files after each run.
Review where files are stored before use.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
